lines: Progressive memory loss, visual hallucinations, and gait instability with falls

She reports that over the past year, he has been experiencing progressive memory loss, visual hallucinations, and episodes of staring into space.
Recently, he has also developed a shuffling gait and has had two falls without loss of consciousness.
His wife denies any fluctuation in his level of consciousness or lucid intervals.

encounters.cc: Displaced femoral neck fracture with postoperative flaccid paralysis

lines: Displaced femoral neck fracture with postoperative flaccid paralysis

This 67-year-old male with Parkinson disease dementia and a history of gait instability with falls previously assessed in Neurology two months prior, returns for inpatient management following orthopedic surgery.
He is admitted to the hospital following surgical repair of a displaced femoral neck fracture sustained during a fall at home.
Postoperatively, he is kept non–weight-bearing on the affected side for 6 weeks to allow for osseous healing.
Due to ongoing pain, limited mobility, and fear of falling again, the patient spends most of his time in bed and has been reluctant to engage in physical therapy sessions.
Over the past few weeks, the nurses have noticed that the patient has become weaker, especially in his lower extremities, and now requires assistance with transfers and repositioning.
He has a history of hypertension, osteopenia, and mild cognitive impairment.
- Open reduction and internal fixation of right femoral neck fracture
- Polyethylene glycol 3350 17 g PO daily as needed
- Calcium carbonate with Vitamin D3 500 mg/200 IU PO twice daily
- Father with hypertension and coronary artery disease
- Mother with osteoporosis and hip fracture
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 15 years ago, 20 pack-year history.
Occupation: Retired high school mathematics teacher.
Repeat physical examination reveals significant bilateral thigh muscle wasting compared to admission, despite stable nutritional intake and no new neurologic deficits.
Lab results are within normal limits, including creatine kinase and electrolytes.
The clinical team attributes his decline to prolonged disuse of skeletal muscle.
